# NOTES (compacted; two books)

## BOOK 1: "The Meddler" by W. C. Tuttle (Gutenberg 79212; orig. Adventure Magazine, Dec 1 1927)

**Setting:** Pineville, Stormy River County. Hashknife Hartley and Sleepy Stevens are drifters.

**Key people**
- **Pat Lynch**: sheriff, small, wiry, sharp-faced, graying.
- **Oscar Johnson**: deputy, tall, thin, sad face, ill-fitting black suit, stiff collar, red four-in-hand tie, too-small boots. Wrecked sheriff's buggy ($160, Cheyenne, yellow wheels) at culvert outside town with Annie Hall (daughter of blacksmith Sam Hall), after a Garnet dance. Annie limped home.
- **Buck Dennig**: TD co-owner/foreman, 10 yrs earlier drifted in at 23 with a bankroll, partnered with Cleve Tolman. Killed behind Stormy River Saloon by small corral: back of head smashed, face down. His tall sorrel tied on far side of corral.
- **Mort Heffner**: prosecuting attorney; sallow, celluloid collar, cameo cuff buttons; lazy, sleepy after all-night poker.
- **Hootie Cooper**: merchant, thin, huge nose, squeaky voice; store rival of Lester Cline ("except kerosene"; his store burned from kerosene).
- **Frank Shell**: gambler, runs Stormy River Saloon.
- **Lester Cline**: younger merchant.
- **Dobe Severn, Bud Hough**: TD cowboys.
- **Dr. (coroner)**: old cow-town doctor, short of speech.
- **Cleve Tolman**: TD co-owner, big, square-jawed, short-spoken, director of Pineville Bank, poor gambler.
- **Shorty Gallup**: TD cowboy (later foreman); ~35, 5'6", stringy colorless hair, pale blue eyes, crooked nose, picks fights.
- **Matt Sturgis**: Shorty's bunkie, tall, thin, grimy, holster tied down.
- **Luke Jones**: TD cook, old, blunt, hates Shorty; "spav," "sheep waddy."
- **Eddie Grimes**: TD puncher, technical; once worked for Blanco; defends Tex.
- **Alex McLean**: TD puncher; brother sick at Wallgate.
- **Tex Blanco** (Bryan): B Arrow owner, just over 6 ft, Spanish blood, coal-black hair graying at temples, gray Stetson with Spanish silver band, blue silk shirt, red silk handkerchief, multicolored sash, wide cartridge belt, gray trousers in fancy high-heeled boots; sorrel with silver-decorated saddle; pearl-handled .45 Colt. Mother Irish (Mary Bryan, from Wexford, white hair, cob pipe, ~69).
- **Frank Judd**: Tex's right-hand man; ~Shorty's height, few lbs lighter. **Tommy Corbett**, **Kit Carson** (B Arrow hands).
- **Guy Shearer**: bank cashier, ~40, stocky, glasses.
- **John Rice**: bank president, small, gray-haired, slightly crippled.
- **Sears**: cattle-association detective from Cheyenne; slender, ~40, grim.
- **Marion Evans**: from Chicago via Cheyenne; new Pineville schoolteacher; first school. Brother Blaine (older) left home at 14 after robbery suspicion. Mother died; Marion earned $5/wk at 15, night school, arrived in Cheyenne with one silver dollar.
- **Windy March**: stage driver; thin, parchment-tanned, tobacco chew, shy with women; named after Buck said "March came in like a lion, went out like a lamb" after two waddies beat him in Stormy River Saloon. Has $83 in Pineville Bank.
- **Mrs. Gladys "Ma" Cooper**: Hootie's wife, huge (240 lbs; once 175 — "shucked Gladys"), kind, sharp-tongued; twelve rose bushes "twelve apostles" (cow ate Matthew, Mark, Luke, John).
- **Sam Hall**: blacksmith, nasal voice, red-tipped nose, school trustee; cat riddle (8 corners, 7 cats each; answer 72).
- **Henry (Hennery) Goff**: postmaster, trustee, querulous.
- **Old Man Beebee**: trustee, bald, sour; wife (Mrs. Beebee) and children Joe and Mary Beebee.
- **Mrs. Hall** (Ella Hall, tattletale, Sam's family).
- **Jimmy Hastings**: ~6-7, freckled, blue eyes, son of Andy Hastings (B Arrow hand; wife dead ~2 yrs). Calls Tex "Uncle Tex." Says "'At's good."
- **Andy Hastings**: B Arrow hand, lean, drives buckboard.
- **Hashknife Hartley**: tall, slender, long serious face, level gray eyes, wide mouth; detective (cattle association; secretly from Milk River, Montana; father a minister). Says he's from "Piney Lake."
- **Sleepy Stevens**: broad-shouldered, square jaw, merry wrinkles, blue eyes; from Idaho; always "jumping at conclusions."
- **Victor / Godfrey**: not in this book.
- **Ben & Bill**: outlaws (Book 2 only).
- **Doctor Brent**: Pineville doctor.
- **Mrs. Allen**: Shearer's landlady.
- **Mr. Long**: replacement teacher (from Garnet).
- **Billings** (Ed Billings, XOX ranch, Wallgate): buys TD; Heffner handles.
- **Old Doctor Brent**, **Windy**, **Alex McLean**, **Dobe**.
- **Hootie's brother Jim Cooper** of Mizpah, Arizona (fake).

**Sequence**
1. Sunday dawn in Pineville; Oscar and Pat argue about buggy. Oscar finds body. Sheriff and Oscar go to saloon. Poker players: Buck left ~1:45–2 a.m. (Hootie: "quarter of two"). Quarrel: Buck accused Tex of stealing a card; Tex left ~1 a.m. leaving ~$60 chips uncashed (Shell holds). Heffner: Buck had roll of bills fastened with rubber band. Coroner; body to his office.
2. Heffner: not enough evidence to arrest Tex. Sheriff relieved.
3. Background of TD and Tolman/Buck; TD ranch 5 mi SW on Lobo Creek.
4. TD crew hears news (Dobe and Bud). Shorty suggests Blanco. Eddie defends Tex; Luke/Shorty feud.
5. Tolman at coroner's; sheriff asks if Buck had quarrel lately — Tolman stares. Shell: Tolman "knows something."
6. Tex and Judd ride into town. Sheriff urges Tex to leave to avoid TD; Tex: "I usually do my runnin' straight ahead."
7. Shearer: Buck drew **$10,000** by check the afternoon before. Buck had $165 on him. Tolman denies knowing (blinks, 10 seconds). No company account; Buck had own account.
8. Marion boards stage at Garnet; Windy's talk; Chicago; Blanco package (Colt Company six-shooters); Tex introduced; trustees (Hootie, Sam Hall, Hennery Goff). Tex's "Nice lookin' feller." Ma Cooper & Marion meet.
9. Marion's family history. Sam's cat riddle. School opens: ~40 pupils. Tex brings Jimmy Hastings on saddle; bet: $50 vs Jimmy with Hastings; Tex wins right to bring Jimmy for a month. Tex says "happiest week." Tolman and two men ride past Marion in dust.
10. Ma Cooper: "Gambled for a chance to see you twice a day."
11. Detective Sears interviews Tolman (Tolman angry; storms out with Shorty). Sears receives note: "We will give you eight hours to leave this valley. —THE BUNCH." Sears leaves by stage with Windy; warned out. Heffner compares "B" in "Bunch" with Tex's B on bank card: similar.
12. Ella Hall: Beebee kids pulled out because Tex visits. Tex says he'll stop coming; Jimmy: "I shore told Ella Hall where to head in at."
13. Trustees (Hootie resigns; Old Man Beebee appointed). Trustees wait at school; Tex doesn't come. Joe Beebee vs Jimmy pencil box fight; Jimmy: "I don't let nobody run a blazer on you."
14. Marion, Ma Cooper to Garnet shopping; stage robbed at mesa (Windy; $3,000 in twenty-dollar gold certificates). Ma & Marion see the holdup from above. Marion finds Tex's pearl-handled Colt in tracks spot; they hide it in her trunk. Sheriff and Oscar find woman's tracks (small foot, high heels).
15. Tolman names Shorty foreman; Luke sulks; Eddie quits after Shorty slaps him with rope; Eddie leaves with Hashknife and Sleepy (who came "over divide from Piney Lake" — lie; Alex McLean saw them at Wallgate three days before).
16. Shorty vs Frank Judd at Stormy River; Oscar takes both guns; Shorty loses teeth; Judd wins.
17. Hashknife & Sleepy at Stormy River; sheriff suspicious. Hootie: Hashknife lies he knows Jim Cooper of Mizpah, Arizona. Sheriff wires Jim; reply: "Never knew anybody by the name of Hashknife Hartley in my life." Hashknife admits lie; sign-blowing anecdote.
18. Sheriff at Coopers' supper accuses Marion of tracks; Ma Cooper says "compounding a felony." Hashknife on porch overhears Marion tell Tex she found his gun at holdup; Tex says "Bless your heart, of course I swear it." Marion's brother = Blaine Evans (later revealed as Buck's identity).
19. Sheriff & Hashknife: second warning note (same as Sears). Shearer's bank vault cleaned ($25,000); Shearer dead (rope with copper wire end, cut end; key ring). Hashknife finds **hondo** marked B with arrow, pockets it. Doctor Brent; Mrs. Blanco and Jimmy typhoid-like fever; Tex sings "My Wild Irish Rose."
20. Luke Jones drunk, fired; Shorty and Matt drunk shoot. Marion fired; Mr. Long hired. Marion goes to B Arrow (Andy's buckboard). Ma Cooper sends trunk via Oscar; Oscar dumps trunk in Stormy River; finds Tex's pearl-handled .45 and swaps its handles with his own (initials "O. J.").
21. Sheriff learns of switch; plan to get gun back. Hashknife overhears. Night visit to B Arrow: shooting. Sleepy shot (unconscious), Tex shot through left shoulder. Hashknife produces gun; "O.J." on trigger guard. Tex's story: knocked out in stable, gagged, blindfolded; gun taken.
22. Hashknife at Garnet: Tolman shoots Luke Jones at Overland Saloon; Luke: Tolman and Buck quarreled; Tolman wanted "Ten thousand down"; Buck had mother and sister. Hashknife hears Luke's blackmail claim ($1,000).
23. Hashknife tells sheriff; sheriff confesses Tex's gun found; Hashknife warns of Windy/money plot. Hashknife: Marion said she was Buck's relative. Tex & Marion on porch.
24. Shorty says nothing; Dobe and Bud leaving for XOX (Billings buying TD). Tolman sale at Heffner's office; Hashknife reveals Marion is Blaine Evans's sister ("Buck Dennig was my brother"). Sale stopped.
25. Tolman tries to shoot Luke Jones on street; Luke shoots Tolman with coat-concealed gun; Tolman dies. Shorty & Matt confess: Shorty killed Buck; Shearer forged Buck's check; split three ways; Shearer killed; money (~$38,000) hidden at TD; Hashknife is detective.
26. Tex freed; Marion and Tex ride home; Judd told to ride with them (Hashknife's order). Ends.

## BOOK 2: "Girl Scouts in Arizona and New Mexico" by Lillian Elizabeth Roy (1923, Grosset & Dunlap)

**Cast**
- **Mrs. Vernon ("Verny")**: Captain of Dandelion Troop.
- **Mr. Vernon ("Unk Verny")**: her husband.
- **Mr. Gilroy ("Gilly", "Gilly-of-the-Dandelioners")**: host, Adirondack estate owner, hiker; saved after Blue Beard's cave.
- **Juliet "Julie" Lee**: Leader; twin of Betty; sister May; writes for *Elmertown Record*; photographer; ambitious writer.
- **Betty ("Betsy") Lee**: twin, timid.
- **Joan ("Jo") Allison**: Corporal.
- **Hester Wynant ("Hesty"/"Hessie")**: camera; "Hesty."
- **Anne Bailey**: big eater; sister Eleanor's wedding.
- **Amy Ward**: mother Mrs. Ward relents later.
- **Judith ("Judy") Blake** and **Edith Blake**: Mrs. Blake (forbidding).
- **Ruth Bentley**: Europe trip.
- **Mary**: Irish maid.
- **Phil Morton**: Elmertown associate editor.
- **Tally**: Indian guide ("Mees Jule"; "Boss" = Gilroy; speaks broken English).
- **Omney**: other guide, went with English party.
- **Tom "Sandy" Sanderson**: Forest Ranger, graduate of Univ. of Albuquerque; horse Snubby; sweet on Julie.
- **Mr. Burt**: newspaper correspondent on Pueblo Indians; Bursum Bill.
- **Ranger Johnson**, **Oliver**: Rangers at Grass Mountain / Panchuelo.
- **Mr. Balmore**: Denver gentleman at Laguna.
- **Mr. Walters**: manager of El Navajo hotel, Gallup.
- **Lorenzo ("Lo", Lorenzo Hubbell)**: Navajo guide.
- **Victor Adair & Godfrey Chase**: college graduates (New York).
- **Padre Miguel**: aged priest, 88.
- **John Sweetwater**: Navajo lad at mission.
- **Bass Guide**: at Grand Canyon.

**Animals**: White Star (Julie's pony, white face spot), Sweetie (Joan's), Stick (Tally's mule), burros Slow Poke (tents), Spark (stove), Good-fer-Nuttin' / Nuttin' (packs). Joan's horse runs wild in sandstorm.

**Sequence**

**Ch 1 – Plans.** Mrs. Vernon's group (Julie, Betty, Joan, Hester). Gilroy's letter (typewritten, facetious): travel light; elk-skin boots; "Chicago Limited" from Philadelphia Sunday; meet Chicago Monday; Gallinas Canyon ice. Ruth to Paris; Anne's sister's wedding last week in July; Mrs. Blake refuses; Mrs. Ward listens to Mrs. Blake. Postcards to home scouts. Dining-room ice-cream.

**Ch 2 – Julie's Secret Ambition.** Sunday train to Philadelphia; Gilroy at Chicago station singing "Oh, say, can you see." Taxi, lunch, Edgewater Beach tea. Pullman night: Julie writes for *Elmertown Record* (her secret). Kansas City. La Junta: Tally. Trinidad; Gilroy's catechism of outfits (khaki, wool, slickers, rubber boots, hiking shoes, riding boots). Elk-skin boots from Indian family (Tally's contact); extra $10 bill to seller; moccasins for home scouts.

**Ch 3 – On the Old Santa Fé Trail.** Horse trader: 9 ponies, 3 burros, $20–30/month, freight from Gallup/Flagstaff/Williams. Insurance. Ponies named (see above). Forest Ranger Tom Sanderson meets them on Raton; fishing; Sandy leaves. Falls near Raton. Julie poses on crooked pine over cliff, falls; Tally rescues (ledge); ammonia from Mrs. Vernon's knapsack. Julie: "I did that very stunt." Hester's camera film used up. Note left on stick for Ranger.

**Ch 4 – Julie Makes a Conquest.** Tally takes wrong trail; lake at night. Sandy arrives at 1 a.m., Snubby whinnies; Sandy slept in camp. Morning: Julie swims; fish; Julie flirts with Sandy. Sandy joins party; Spanish-speaking; Julie describes Phil Morton; Joan teases. Pecos legends; Springer by evening.

**Ch 5 – Sandy Has His Say.** Springer: Burt (newspaper) missed; Sandy sent to Las Vegas. Tally sent by freight with burros; disapproves. Wagon Mound, Optimo, Valmora, Watrous; Mora Canyon. Castañeda Hotel. Reading-room debate: Sandy vs Burt on Bursum Bill, Mescalero/National Park bill, 1913 Supreme Court ruling; water rights. Julie writes secret letter to Burt/Record.

**Ch 6 – Pecos Forests.** Las Vegas (3 cities: Spanish, Castañeda, Hot Springs). Gallinas canyon ice (60,000 tons). Pecos Forest 750,000 acres. Sandy won't hunt for sport. Bernal Creek; Blanchard; Pecos town (adobe). Ranger Johnson leads up Pecos Canyon; Apache Inn at Valley Ranch; Grass Mountain; Oliver's station. Tally's Beaver & Porcupine legend (told to Julie; she writes it up).

**Ch 7 – Where Are the Burros?** Lake Park; burros hobbled; Panchuelo. Burros stolen; two men drove them down-trail; pipe ash. Tally scouts; Bishop's Lodge; Sandy arrives, hides behind newspaper; goes to Santa Fé to get guides/forest detectives. Gilroy & Tally return past midnight.

**Ch 8 – Gilly Turns Forest Ranger.** Gilroy's account: smoke/forest fire near Winsor; Rangers Oliver & Johnson; fire-fighting (100,000 acres; spades, axes, mats); fire quenched; burros/Tally unfound.

**Ch 9 – Tally and the Rustlers.** Tally's moccasins; creeps; captures Ben (tied) and Bill (Colt, rope); burros; old camp smoldering; forest fire; Tally drives outlaws; back to Bishop's Lodge. Reward (New Yorkers' horses; $500). Sandy brings two New Yorkers' horses; outlaws jailed.

**Ch 10 – Ancient Ruins and Modern Romance.** Adair and Chase join party. Tesuque, Cuyamunque, Nambe Falls, Escondillo, Sanctuario, Chimayo blankets, Truchas, Trampas, Ranchos de Taos (Taos pueblo 7 stories). Betty: "Verny, what do you mean?" Puye Ruins (1600 rooms). Belnap Ranch near Santa Fé.

**Ch 11 – Padre Miguel's Story.** Padre Miguel (88, toothless). Old Palace; Spanish lady's justice; Fonda and customs jail (bullet holes); caravan imagery; Isleta friar's body. Sandy & Burt get info. Mr. Vernon & Gilroy agree to hire automobiles (Mr. Vernon secretly wrote fathers). Two cars hired (Sandy bargains).

**Ch 12 – Julie's Tête-à-Tête.** Jemez cliff dwellings; Frijoles Canyon (Painted Cave); Cañon de Cochita; San Felipe; Tiffany turquoise; Ortiz placers; Chaco Canyon; Aztec ruins. Surprise: Anne Bailey, Judith, Amy arrive by train at Santa Fé (Julie's articles changed Mrs. Ward). Albuquerque: Alvarado Hotel; University of New Mexico; hop-dance. Sandy and Julie balcony: wants letters, not post-cards; Julie plans to write; "Here's my post office address—Julie, dear!"

**Ch 13 – The Enchanted Mesa.** Sandy leaves; Burt continues to Gallup. Laguna; Mr. Balmore; wagon-team; Julie snapshot; mirage (mountain vanishes); Acoma pueblo (church 40 years, walls 10 ft thick). Council: Arizona one month; Petrified Forest, Grand Cañon, Hualapai; Salt River, Gila, Apache Trail, Roosevelt Dam, Tucson; Sunset Route to Houston → Galveston steamer → New York.

**Ch 14 – At St. Michael's Mission.** Conductor advises Cañon de Chelly and White House. Gallup, El Navajo hotel; Mr. Walters (manager) advises selling burros in Gallup, buying Navajo pack-horses ($25–30). Gilroy's contract: leave burros in Gallup. Freight at midnight. Tally hesitant; Gilroy & Vernon go with Tally. Cars carry tents/stove on rack. Drive through Navajo land; Painted Desert view. St. Michael's Mission: Father; Mother Superior; Navajo school; vespers; supper; John Sweetwater's "White Feather" tent puzzle; Nature Game.

**Ch 15 – The Painted Desert.** Julie's letter to Sandy (Captain: no endearments). Lo (Lorenzo); Ganado (Hubbell's Mission House, "King of Northern Arizona"); sheep, hogans; San Francisco Mountains; sage; cedar forest; water-pool; night cold. Sandstorm (simoon): Joan's horse slides into gravel pit; Joan saves horse; Ream's Cañon (Kit Carson monument; school for Navajo/Moki). Moki villages on tufa. Gilroy quotes Cobb's "I shall not try it." Lo refuses to go beyond Navajo Land. Adamana; horses rest; Gilroy's decision.

**Ch 16 – Region of the Petrified Forests.** Gilroy's flood story (trees petrified). First forest: Eagle's Head, Petrified Bridge (111 ft). Second (2,000 acres), Chalcedony Park, Rainbow Forest. Julie's Record articles: Sunset Crater; Meteorite Mountain (200 ft mound, 1 mile bowl, 40 acres); Cañon Diablo (bridge 250 ft). Refused: Betatakin/Kitsiel, Hopi villages, Walnut Cañon, Montezuma's Castle (47 miles south of Flagstaff). Lowell Observatory at night. Trinidad telegram: "Ship back freight collect." Horses sent home. Tally sells 3 pack-horses at Williams for $30 each ($90); outfits; 50-50 split. Gilroy: "Gilly turning horse-trader!"

**Ch 17 – Bright Angel Trail.** Train to Grand Cañon; sarcastic tourist. Sunset from rail; purple shadows. John Bass camp (Gilroy says no room service). Sunrise; bacon; Betty afraid; scouts go anyway. Bright Angel trail: 23 tourists; woman (Lizzie) insists on going back; Julie's mule on corner (half over edge); Indian Gardens; Jacob's Ladder; Devil's Corkscrew; Phantom Ranch; Bright Angel Creek; Ribbon Falls. Julie's film; bird and plant records (240 bird species; cacti; ocotillo "Devil's Claw"; Arizona dandelion). Mail for Julie: letters forwarded from Sandy (two postmarked "Glorieta, New Mexico"). Gilroy's telegram: lawyer; Adirondack estate title; court opens September; party returns east by train. Tally: "Don' leaf Tally outen dat mountain climb." Ends: Julie "So _he_ says."
